content.title: About
content.content: A Bologna sandwich on wheat bread is a classic sandwich made with slices of cooked Bologna sausage, fresh vegetables, and sauce, placed between two slices of whole‑grain wheat bread. It is popular in Europe and the United States as a quick snack or light meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bologna sausage gets its name from the Italian city of Bologna, where it is traditionally made from beef, pork and spices.
The first recorded recipe for a sandwich with Bologna dates back to early 19th‑century cookbooks.
Wheat bread provides a slower release of carbohydrates, keeping energy levels steadier than white bread.
The sandwich is often served with mustard or mayonnaise, lettuce, tomato and cucumber.
In some regions cheese such as Emmental or Cheddar is added for extra flavor.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Bologna provides about 12 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Meat supplies heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B6 and B12 aid metabolism and support the nervous system.

items.title: Dietary fiber from whole‑grain bread
items.content: Whole‑grain wheat bread adds fiber that promotes digestive health.

items.title: Antioxidant content
items.content: Vitamin E present in the fat used for the sausage helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Processed meats often contain a lot of salt, which can raise blood pressure if consumed in excess.

items.title: Nitrites and preservatives
items.content: Nitrites are used to preserve color and shelf life; large amounts are considered potentially harmful.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to components of the sausage.

items.title: Calorie dense
items.content: A sandwich can contain 300–450 kcal, so portion control is advisable for weight‑management diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Assemble the sandwich by layering slices of Bologna, lettuce, thinly sliced tomato and cucumber between two pieces of whole‑grain wheat bread. Add mustard, mayo or a yogurt‑based sauce if desired. It can be eaten by hand or cut into smaller pieces for children.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared sandwich refrigerated at 0–4 °C and consume within 24 hours. Store the sausage in its original packaging or an airtight container, and keep the bread in a dry place or sealed bag to prevent drying out.
